headline: Going Commando reaches 15.46% matched code for USA v1.01
summary: Going Commando's refreshed progress report takes USA v1.01 from 14.04% to 15.46% matched code, with 4,618 of 8,584 functions. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. The other releases reach 11.24% and 3,867 of 8,678 functions for Europe/Australia v1.00, and 14.63% and 4,413 of 8,639 for USA v2.00. Landed work includes 129 verified implementations carried from a fork, movement helpers and boot functions (#329, #328, #332).
highlights: The fork carry-over leaves out a command-byte reader whose exact version required explicit register bindings and an empty compiler barrier (#329).
A shared level helper matches in all 27 tested placements (#331). Its author reports that a broader unit-test run was blocked by compiler sandbox errors.
Three large Oozla, Dobbo and Snivelak reconstructions gain corrected storage and lifetime details, but remain outside the linked build (#330).
